title: MAGE model system
description: A model system: one identity namespace of entities, zero or more graph models, zero or more state machines. Shape only -- meaning is fixed by SEMANTICS.md, whose validation rules V1-V31 this schema cannot all express. Rules marked ENGINE below require a validator pass beyond JSON Schema.

mage.description: Format version. Incompatible changes bump it.

values.description: Required for enum / ordered-enum. For ordered-enum the list order IS the order, ascending.

description.description: What the presence of this relation asserts. For humans.

absence.description: What the ABSENCE of this relation asserts -- often the more important half. For humans.

path.description: allowed: multi-hop queries over this relation are licensed (transitive closure is a legitimate object of inquiry). forbidden: the engine REFUSES such queries (V7). This is not a claim that the relation itself is transitive.

aggregates.description: Declares that an AUTHORED property on the source is the aggregate of a property read off each target (V45, V46). v0.1 computes nothing over a relation, so the value stays written on the entity; this declaration is what lets the validator reject a disagreement instead of leaving the edge layer decorative.

declared.description: The property on the SOURCE entity carrying the authored aggregate.

over.description: The property read off each TARGET entity and aggregated.

using.description: The aggregation operator. A closed set of one: a permissive vocabulary cannot be narrowed again without breaking every model that relied on it.

acyclic.description: true makes a cycle in this relation type a validation error (V8).

entities.description: THE identity namespace. Ids are immutable (V2); labels are not.

properties.description: IMMUTABLE descriptive facts. Never part of the state vector (V16).

events.description: Declared synchronized events (tier T3). An event is ONE system transition involving all participants, applied atomically.

participants.description: Machine names. Every participant must offer a sync:-transition for this event (V12). A multiply-instantiated participant is REFUSED in v0.1 (V14).

machines.description: Behavioral units. One instance unless instances: is declared. A machine need not correspond to an entity; where it does, say so with entity:.

entity.description: Optional correspondence to a system entity (V6).

instances.description: N independent interleaved copies, addressed name[0..N-1]. Default 1, addressed by bare name. Gives occupancy, NOT binding (V14).

variables.description: THE state vector. Every variable must have a FINITE domain (V17).

derived.description: Pure expressions over current state. Never stored, never part of state identity (V18); dependency graph must be acyclic (V19).

models.description: Purposeful reductions over the entity namespace.

entities.description: Ids of system-level entities this model includes. Models reference; they never redeclare (V3).

quantities.description: Quantitative annotations over existing semantic objects. NEVER part of the behavioral state vector (V6/SEMANTICS.md 5.2) -- a real-valued annotation in the state vector would make the reachable space infinite. ENGINE-checked: targets resolve (V27), dimension and literals are readable (V28), magnitudes are in bounds (V29), dimensions agree (V30), each one reaches an analysis (V36, V37).

accounting.description: How each path-aggregated metric charges its annotations, keyed by metric name (`latency`, `cost`). One basis per metric; the vocabulary is `entities` for v0.1, closed so that adding transition or relation accounting is a deliberate act. Declared per quantitative model -- v0.1 has one per system, the quantities: map, so this is a top-level block. ENGINE-checked (V35): the metric and the basis are known, and a metric with annotations declares one. NEITHER the metric name nor the basis is enumerated here, for the reason `dimension` is not: a wrong one reaches the MEANING layer and both implementations cite V35 instead of Python answering SCHEMA where TypeScript answers a V-number.

queries.description: Saved queries, re-run when the model changes. Each value conforms to mage-query.schema.json.

requirements.description: Obligations the system under design is judged against, keyed by id. A requirement references the POSITIVE breach query by id and declares the proposition value that discharges it (`satisfied_when: refuted` for a prohibition stated as its existential dual, `holds` for a universal stated directly). The query is NEVER negated internally to make the requirement read positively. A requirement carries no verdict and no status: what the models say is a query result, and what the pair MEANS is a verification (satisfied/violated/inconclusive/error), derived per read and stored nowhere. NEITHER `satisfied_when`'s vocabulary nor `expressed_as`'s join is enumerated or resolved here, for the reason `accounting`'s metric name is not: a wrong word reaches the MEANING layer, where `parseRequirement` says why `inconclusive` and `unlicensed` cannot discharge an obligation and a dangling `expressed_as` verifies as `error`, instead of JSON Schema answering SHAPE where the engine has a sentence.

additionalProperties.$comment: A requirement carries no `notes:`, deliberately. The declaration enters systemHash (it is authored content that changes what the system prescribes), and a note inside it would hash with it -- which invariant A1 forbids, since annotation never alters interpretation or an analysis result. The prescription's own prose is `statement`, so nothing is lost.

statement.description: The obligation in the modal voice -- "Restricted data must not reach an impermitted subscriber." Prescriptive, where a query's `name` is descriptive and a model's `purpose.question` is interrogative; the three are distinct sentences and none is derived from another.

expressed_as.description: The saved query that decides this obligation, by id. A join rather than an inlined query: one query can decide several obligations, and inlining would duplicate it.

satisfied_when.description: Shape only -- a string. The two-word vocabulary (`holds`, `refuted`) lives in the engine, which is also where a YAML 1.1 loader's coercion of `no` to a boolean gets the sentence citing V25.

views.description: Visual reductions. A view is itself a purposeful reduction; it carries NO semantic model data.

layout.description: Optional position HINTS for incremental layout stability. Never semantic.

id.description: Shape only. Ids that a YAML 1.1 loader would coerce (on/off/yes/no/true/false/null/~, or numeric-looking) are additionally REFUSED by the validator (V25) -- this pattern cannot catch them because the loader mangles them first.

quantity.description: One quantitative annotation. Shape only. NOTE what is deliberately NOT constrained here: `dimension` carries no enum and `target` carries no prefix pattern, so an unrecognised dimension or target kind reaches the MEANING layer and both implementations cite the same rule (V28/V27) instead of Python answering SCHEMA where TypeScript answers a V-number. Nor is value-or-range required: V28's message tells an author what to write, which a oneOf complaint does not.

target.description: `<kind>:<ref>` over the closed kind set transition | relation | entity | state | parameter | model (V27). A transition is addressed `transition:<machine>#<index>` -- it has no id, and label: carries no semantics (V1). A relation is addressed by its own id:.

dimension.description: One of duration | memory | cost | ratio | count. Checked at the meaning layer (V28), not here.

value.description: A unit-bearing literal (`250 ms`), a bare number for the dimensionless dimensions ratio and count, or an expression. A unit-bearing literal is a STRING in YAML, which is why its magnitude is parsed by the workbench rather than by a loader: the two loaders this project runs disagree on `017`, `1_000`, `1e3` and `1:30`.

expression.description: A sum of products over literals, `metrics.*` values and other quantity ids. Operators stand alone between spaces, because an id may contain `-`. No parentheses in v0.1.

range.description: A closed interval, low then high (V29). Both ends carry the same dimension (V30).

residency.description: `resident` -- charged in every configuration where the target exists. Exactly one of residency / when on a configuration-scoped (memory) quantity; neither is a finding, because the quantity would then enter no summand of memory(c) (V37). NO enum here deliberately: `residency: transient` is a plausible author guess and V37's message names the closed vocabulary, which a schema complaint does not.

when.description: `{ state: <machine>.<state> }` -- charged exactly while that behavioral state is active. The state reference resolves like any other (V27). Left OPEN rather than closed to `state` only, for the reason a note object is left open: an unexpected key here means the charge is declared nowhere, and V37 can say that where a shape complaint cannot.

domain.description: Names a domain in domains:. Required for order comparisons (V20).

type.description: ref is RESERVED and must be rejected with a future-version message, never misinterpreted (V15).

label.description: Documentation only. Carries NO semantics -- use sync: for synchronization (V1).

sync.description: Synchronization, and nothing else. MUST resolve to an entry in events: (V1).

requires.description: Guard over the PRE-transition system state, evaluated atomically with the transition. A guard is NOT synchronization: it reads another machine without making it step. Refused against a multiply-instantiated machine (V11).

effects.description: Variable assignments. Two transitions joined by one event MUST NOT assign the same variable (V13) -- statically checked from this block.

purpose.description: What this reduction is FOR. omits is CHECKED against the model's actual vocabulary, not merely asserted (V24).

notes.description: Free annotation attached to an entity, a model or a relation. NON-SEMANTIC: notes never alter interpretation or an analysis result, and the canonical hash excludes them (A1, SEMANTICS.md 5.1).

note.description: One note. OPEN on purpose: an unquoted comma in YAML flow style truncates the text and leaves a stray KEY behind, and the validator reports that under ANNOTATION with the cause named. A shape complaint about an unexpected property would be the same unhelpful message V25 exists to replace.

kind.description: assumption is the interesting one: a note SAYING something is an assumption does not make it part of formal analysis. To constrain a query it must be represented as a property, variable, guard or quantity.

author.description: Which side wrote it -- human or agent. Not an identity claim.

at.description: Timestamp, QUOTED. JSON has no date type and a bare one is coerced by a YAML 1.1 loader (10.1).

historyEntry.description: One entry of a provenance history. Append-only and system-managed, never editable commentary.

provenance.description: Where an object came from, in both senses one key has to carry: what part of the world it corresponds to (subject / correspondence, 8.1), and who authored it (created_by / prompt / history, 5.1). Non-semantic like notes.

prompt.description: The instruction that produced this object -- the field that earns provenance its place. With agent-authored models it answers why the model has this shape, which reading the model cannot tell you. Deliberately not the whole conversation.

kind.description: How the model-to-world correspondence was established. v0.1 permits asserted; the stronger kinds are where later tooling earns trust rather than claiming it.
